source_refs.note: Exercise 9.2, Question 10 (book p. 273); the book prints no answers for Exercise 9.2; answers checked with sympy and the solution book

blocks.explanation:
Yahan har term mein ek inverse angle ka squared trigonometric function hai, aur jawab ek number hai.
Diya kya hai? \(\sec^{2}\) of \(\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{4}\) aur \(\csc^{2}\) of \(\cot^{-1}\frac{2}{5}\).
Find kya karna hai? Jama \(\frac{889}{400}\) dikhana hai.
Rule kaunsa? Pythagorean identities \(1 + \tan^{2}\alpha = \sec^{2}\alpha\) aur \(1 + \cot^{2}\beta = \csc^{2}\beta\).
Plan: angles ko naam do, identity se har square nikalo, phir fractions jama karo.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\sec^{2}\left(\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{4}\right) + \csc^{2}\left(\cot^{-1}\frac{2}{5}\right)\).
Maloom karna (prove): yeh \(\frac{889}{400}\) ke barabar hai.
Tareeqa: andar wala inverse humein seedha \(\tan\alpha\) aur \(\cot\beta\) bata deta hai. Phir identities \(\sec^{2}\alpha = 1 + \tan^{2}\alpha\) aur \(\csc^{2}\beta = 1 + \cot^{2}\beta\) se squares mil jate hain. Squares ki wajah se na koi square root, na sign ka sawal; yeh is sawal ki khoobi hai.

Pehla term
\[\alpha = \tan^{-1}\tfrac{1}{4},\quad \tan\alpha = \tfrac{1}{4}\]
\[\sec^{2}\alpha = 1 + \tan^{2}\alpha = 1 + \tfrac{1}{16}\]
\[= \tfrac{17}{16}\]
Kyun: \(\sin^{2}\alpha + \cos^{2}\alpha = 1\) ko \(\cos^{2}\alpha\) se divide karein to \(\tan^{2}\alpha + 1 = \sec^{2}\alpha\) milta hai. \(\tan^{2}\alpha = \frac{1}{16}\), to \(\sec^{2}\alpha = \frac{17}{16}\).

Doosra term
\[\beta = \cot^{-1}\tfrac{2}{5},\quad \cot\beta = \tfrac{2}{5}\]
\[\csc^{2}\beta = 1 + \cot^{2}\beta = 1 + \tfrac{4}{25}\]
\[= \tfrac{29}{25}\]
Kyun: wohi identity, is dafa \(\sin^{2}\beta\) se divide kar ke: \(1 + \cot^{2}\beta = \csc^{2}\beta\).
Dhyan dein: \(\cot\) ke saath \(\csc\) jata hai aur \(\tan\) ke saath \(\sec\); jore ghalat na banaiye.

Jama karein
\[\text{L.H.S} = \tfrac{17}{16} + \tfrac{29}{25}\]
\[= \tfrac{425 + 464}{400} = \tfrac{889}{400} = \text{R.H.S}\]
Kyun: 16 aur 25 ka LCM 400 hai (dono ka koi common factor nahi). \(17 \times 25 = 425\) aur \(29 \times 16 = 464\), jama 889.

Tasdeeq
\[1.0625 + 1.16 = 2.2225\]
\[\tfrac{889}{400} = 2.2225\ \checkmark\]
Kyun: decimals mein bhi dono taraf barabar.
Is sawal mein kisi formula ki shart ka masla nahi tha, kyunke hum ne sirf identities istemal ki, angles jama nahi kiye.
